prompt: Scan the default top-1000 TCP ports of 10.0.0.5
why: Bare nmap = top 1000 TCP ports.

prompt: Scan ALL 65535 TCP ports of 10.0.0.5
why: -p- means every TCP port.

prompt: Detect service versions on 10.0.0.5
why: -sV fingerprints the software/version behind each port.

prompt: Fast SYN (half-open) scan of the 10.0.0.0/24 subnet
why: -sS never finishes the handshake: faster, quieter.

prompt: List listening TCP/UDP sockets with the owning program
why: t=tcp u=udp l=listening p=process n=numeric.

prompt: Show what the current user may run via sudo
why: First thing to check for Linux privesc.

prompt: Find SUID binaries anywhere on the filesystem
why: SUID binaries run as their owner - a privesc hunt.

prompt: List all running processes (full detail)
why: Classic full process listing.

prompt: List every computer in the domain
why: Enumerates all domain-joined machines.

prompt: List all domain controllers
why: DCs are the crown jewels of AD.

prompt: Show the members of Domain Admins
why: Who holds the keys to the domain.

prompt: List members of the local Administrators group
why: Who is admin on THIS box.

prompt: Show listening TCP connections (PowerShell)
why: PowerShell's answer to 'what's exposed here'.

prompt: Show your token's privileges (cmd/PowerShell)
why: SeImpersonate/SeBackup/SeDebug here are privesc gold.

prompt: Find failed-logon events in the Security log
why: Event 4625 = failed logon: spot brute force.

prompt: Crack raw-MD5 hashes in hashes.txt with John and rockyou.txt
why: Tell John the hash format and give it a wordlist.

prompt: Crack MD5 hashes in hashes.txt with hashcat and rockyou.txt
why: -m 0 = MD5, -a 0 = straight wordlist attack.

prompt: Show the passwords John has already cracked for hashes.txt
why: Reads cracked results from the pot file.

prompt: Fetch only the response headers of http://10.0.0.5
why: -I = HEAD request: headers only.

prompt: Make a verbose request to http://10.0.0.5 (show the exchange)
why: -v shows the full request/response, TLS and all.

prompt: Look up the MX (mail) records for example.com
why: MX = which server receives the domain's mail.

prompt: Test the id param of http://10.0.0.5/item?id=1 for SQLi, no prompts
why: --batch takes defaults so it runs unattended.
